# **CFTC and ETF Report** _A weekly update of futures and exchange traded fund activity._ - In our last CFTC report we predicted that any gains for gold beyond $1,640 would be hard-won, and last week’s price action bore out this view. Gold crept higher from an initial low of $1,631, and approached $1,670 by the close on Friday. Physical interest in Asia was greatly reduced in the lead-up to the Chinese New Year holiday, leaving the gold price all the more prone to following trends in currency markets and fluctuations in risk sentiment. Last week’s climb in gold closely mirrored that of the Euro, which recovered from its lowest point since 2010 to gain almost 2.5% on the week. - Silver traded indifferently for much of the week, range-bound between $30.00 and $31.00. It exploded into life on Friday, however, with a sharp move to $32.00. Reports that the Sprott Silver ETF had added 10 million ounces of silver to its holdings helped initiate the buying, and the spike was exacerbated as stops were taken out on the way up. Thanks to this move, silver is currently the bestperforming precious metal in 2012, with gains of more than 17.5% since the beginning of the year. • Platinum continued its strong performance so far this year, adding another $60 last week. It benefitted from the broader improvement in risk sentiment, gaining ground in the face of a weakening US Dollar. The physical market in Asia was quiet as expected in the lead-up to Chinese New Year, but investor buying was sufficient to maintain platinum’s upward trajectory. Platinum has comfortably outperformed gold since the second week of this year, and by the end of last week the gold-platinum spread had narrowed to $135 from an all-time high of $216 on January 6th. • Palladium followed its cousin platinum virtually stepfor-step last week, making highs above $680 on Thursday and closing near this level on Friday to lock in a gain of more than $45 on the week. The one divergence of note came on Wednesday, when palladium broke a downward drift and popped up $25. There were few fundamental drivers in play; by and large, palladium followed risk assets and like platinum, benefitted from US Dollar weakness. #### **David Jollie** **david.jollie@mitprecious.com Tel: +44 20 7489 6767** **24 January 2012** #### **New York:** 200 Park Avenue, New York, NY 10166 0130 Tel: +1 212 878 4122 #### **London:** 4th Floor, St Martins Court, 10 Paternoster Row, London EC4M 7BB Tel: +44 20 7489 6767 #### **Hong Kong:** Suite 1306, Two Exchange Square, 8 Connaught Place, Central, Hong Kong Tel: +852 2899 2026 #### **Tokyo:** 2-1 Ohtemachi 1-Chome, Chiyoda-Ku, Tokyo 100 Tel: +81 33 285 3407 #### **Singapore:** 80 Robinson Road, #15-02, Singapore, 068898 Tel: +65 6372 8050 **Mitsui Global Precious Metals | CFTC and ETF Weekly Report** **24 January 2012** ## **Gold CFTC data to 17 January 2012; ETF data to 20 January 2012.** |**Exchang**|**e (COMEX a**

Gold crept higher from an initial low of $1,631, and approached $1,670 by the close on Friday. Physical interest in Asia was greatly reduced in the lead-up to the Chinese New Year holiday, leaving the gold price all the more prone to following trends in currency markets and fluctuations in risk sentiment. Last week’s climb in gold closely mirrored that of the Euro, which recovered from its lowest point since 2010 to gain almost 2.5% on the week. Yields on German and US 10-year government bonds edged higher as demand softened. The world’s major equities markets boasted solid gains, while the US Dollar lost ground against a basket of other major currencies lost ground, completing the broad picture of improving risk sentiment. - Gold’s positive performance against this risk-on backdrop suggests that the yellow metal has not yet fully reverted to a “safe-haven” role. It seems, however, that the broader risk rally was driven less by genuine bullish confidence than by a spate of short-covering, especially in the Euro. Eurozone debt remains the most pressing issue facing markets at the moment, and there was very little in last week’s news to indicate that the situation is set to improve any time soon. Market consensus is that gold, which has been remarkably quiet in 2012 compared with the other precious metals, is poised for a move higher. If risk sentiment also turns bearish, gold could yet regain some safe-haven allure. - Net long speculative positions on COMEX increased by just over 950,000 ounces—a greater increase than in the previous week, and suggestive of a cautiously bullish market. By contrast, long positions on TOCOM were s

caled back. Net inflows to ETFs were also positive, the SPDR Gold Trust leading the way by adding more than 48,000 ounces last week. ### **Gold Exchange Investment, Jan 10 — Jan 12** 40 2,000 Gold price, $/oz

Thanks to this move, silver is currently the best-performing precious metal in 2012, with gains of more than 17.5% since the beginning of the year. - Net long speculative positions on COMEX increased by 5.5 million ounces - a noticeable slowdown from the previous week’s increase of 14 million ounces. Again, a decline of similar magnitude in open interest suggests that short covering, rather than the opening of fresh long positions, was largely responsible for the increase in net positioning. It should also be noted that due to the frequency with which d

In the options market, the figures show that positions were scaled back slightly in the period January 10th17th—a week in which prices were relatively stagnant. Friday’s move higher sparked a surge in buying interest in 3-4 month upside calls, especially at the $40 strike, suggesting that the market is readying itself for further appreciation. - ETF flows in silver were very quiet aside from the 10 million ounces added by the Sprott fund on Friday.
